record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Determine which functions f in L^2_a(D) have the property that every z-invariant subspace of L^2_a(D) containing f has index 1, where the index of an invariant subspace M is dim(M/zM).

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 15 Determine which f in L2a(D)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space, i.e. the Hilbert space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ such that
$$\|f\|^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure. A closed subspace $M\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called $z$-invariant if $zM\subseteq M$. The index of such a subspace is defined by
$$\operatorname{ind}(M)=\dim(M\ominus zM)=\dim(M/zM).$$
It is known that for every integer $n$ with $1\le n\le\infty$ there exist $z$-invariant subspaces $M\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ with $\operatorname{ind}(M)=n$.

Characterize the functions $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ with the following property: every $z$-invariant subspace $M\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ that contains $f$ satisfies $\operatorname{ind}(M)=1$.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard surveys on Bergman space function theory list the characterization of functions forcing index-one invariant subspaces as an open problem; no published complete characterization was found. Partial results exist (e.g. functions with sufficiently slow growth or in suitable subclasses force index 1), but a full description remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on Bergman space problems including index of invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization problem of which f force index-one is presented as open.

status_evidence.title: Shift Invariant Subspaces Of Large Index In The Bloch Space
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of invariant subspaces of arbitrary index in Bergman-type spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Invariant subspaces of all indices exist, motivating the question of which functions are contained only in index-one subspaces.
